name: Unlearn Your Pain / Mind Body Syndrome program (Howard Schubiner)
founders: Howard Schubiner, MD, FACP (internist/pediatrician; Mind Body Medicine program, Ascension Providence Hospital, Southfield MI; clinical professor, Michigan State University College of Human Medicine; earlier Wayne State University faculty)
Hal Greenham, BSc Psych (Australian pain/somatic psychotherapist; co-creator of the Freedom From Chronic Pain online course)
founded_year_range: Early-to-mid 2000s for the hospital mind-body clinic (estimate, not verified). 2010 for the first self-published edition of the book (not re-verified) and the first RCT (Hsu et al., JGIM 2010, verified). The online course existed by 2021. Penguin Random House / The Open Field trade edition 26 May 2026.
cost_summary: Freedom From Chronic Pain online program (12-month access, checked Oct 2026): USD 297 standard, 397 with individualised support, 497 with one 50-60 min therapist session (or 12 monthly payments of 28/36/45). Money-back guarantee; about 2% refund rate claimed. 2026 hardcover book USD 35. Workbooks are self-published (price not listed). Telehealth consult fees are not published, and insurance is not accepted. The Coursera course is free to audit.
mechanisms: neuroplastic/learned pain (brain-generated danger signal / predictive processing)
autonomic/nervous system dysregulation (sympathetic overdrive, "stuck in fight-or-flight")
mechanism_summary: "Mind Body Syndrome" (later called neuroplastic, primary or nociplastic "neural circuit" disorders): real symptoms produced by learned brain pathways that act as a danger or alarm signal (predictive processing), with no ongoing tissue damage. The alarm is sensitised by childhood adversity, trauma, suppressed emotions (anger, guilt) and traits such as perfectionism. Fear, attention and avoidance keep it going in a pain-fear cycle. One mechanism is applied to pain, IBS, bladder symptoms, fatigue, POTS, anxiety and depression. Patients are differentiated mainly by whether their symptoms are primary or secondary (structural). Primary symptoms are "ruled in" by positive history features; 88.3% of 222 back/neck pain patients were classed as primary in J Pain 2024.
techniques: physician diagnostic consultation to rule out structural disease and 'rule in' mind-body syndrome
pain neuroscience education / reattribution to the brain
daily expressive writing (free writing, unsent letters, dialogues)
talking back to the brain / confident self-statements
somatic tracking and mindful attention to symptoms
graded exposure and resuming avoided activities, deconditioning triggers
emotional awareness and expression (anger, grief, guilt, love), assertiveness
ISTDP- and IFS-informed emotion work (online course)
4-week structured daily program (book); 30-module online course with forum
mainstream_notes: Based in an academic teaching hospital (Ascension Providence/MSU). MSU hosts the Coursera course, and CME credit is offered for viewing the documentary. Derived therapies (EAET, PRT) have been tested in NIH-funded, VA and Karolinska RCTs; the largest is the VA EAET vs CBT trial, JAMA Netw Open 2024 (N=126). PORT for POTS is in pilot at VCU. Schubiner has consulted for UnitedHealth Group, Karuna Labs and Curable (2022 disclosure) and co-authors work on the ICD-11 primary-pain diagnosis. The branded book and course are not named in NICE, CDC or ACP guidelines.
insurance_notes: The book, online course and Schubiner's telehealth are self-pay; the site states the practice does not accept insurance. EAET or PRT delivered by licensed therapists may be billed as standard psychotherapy.

key_trials.citation: Hsu MC, Schubiner H, Lumley MA, Stracks JS, Clauw DJ, Williams DA. J Gen Intern Med 2010;25:1064-70. PMID 20532650
key_trials.design: RCT vs waitlist. Affective self-awareness: 1 physician consult plus 3 weekly 2-h groups. Women with fibromyalgia.
key_trials.finding: At 6 months: lower pain severity, better physical function and higher tender-point threshold. 45.8% had >=30% pain reduction vs 0% of controls.

key_trials.citation: Burger AJ, ..., Schubiner H. J Psychosom Res 2016;81:1-8. PMID 26800632
key_trials.design: Uncontrolled trial. Consult plus 4 groups. Chronic musculoskeletal pain.
key_trials.finding: Large pre-post improvements maintained at 6 months. About 2/3 had >=30% pain reduction and 1/3 had >=70%.

key_trials.citation: Lumley MA, Schubiner H, et al. Pain 2017;158:2354-63. PMID 28796118
key_trials.design: Cluster RCT. EAET vs CBT vs education, 8 x 90-min groups. Fibromyalgia.
key_trials.finding: Primary outcome (pain severity) null vs education. Better on many secondary outcomes. Beat CBT on widespread pain and on >=50% pain reduction (22.5% vs 8.3%).

key_trials.citation: Thakur ER, ..., Schubiner H, Lumley MA. Neurogastroenterol Motil 2017;29:e13143. PMID 28643436
key_trials.design: RCT. EAET vs relaxation vs waitlist, 3 sessions. IBS.
key_trials.finding: EAET, but not relaxation, reduced IBS symptom severity vs waitlist at 10 weeks.

key_trials.citation: Ziadni MS, ..., Schubiner H, Lumley MA. Health Psychol 2018;37:282-90. PMID 29154608
key_trials.design: RCT. Single life-stress emotional awareness/expression interview vs usual care. Medically unexplained symptoms in primary care.
key_trials.finding: Lower pain severity and interference, sleep problems and psychological symptoms at 6 weeks.

key_trials.citation: Carty JN, ..., Schubiner H, Lumley MA. Pain Med 2019;20:1321-9. PMID 30252113
key_trials.design: RCT. Single 90-min interview (n=37) vs usual care (n=25). Women with urogenital pain.
key_trials.finding: Lower pain severity and pelvic-floor symptoms. No effect on pain interference or psychological symptoms.

key_trials.citation: Kohns DJ, Urbanik CP, Geisser ME, Schubiner H, Lumley MA. Clin J Pain 2020;36:683-92. PMID 32520816
key_trials.design: RCT. Brief internet pain psychology and neuroscience self-evaluation vs matched education. Chronic musculoskeletal pain.
key_trials.finding: Small 1-month reductions in pain and interference, mostly in non-fibromyalgia pain. Most effects lost by 10 months.

key_trials.citation: Yarns BC, Lumley MA, ..., Schubiner H, Sultzer DL. Pain Med 2020;21:2811-22. PMID 32451528
key_trials.design: Preliminary RCT. EAET vs CBT. Older veterans with chronic musculoskeletal pain.
key_trials.finding: EAET produced greater pain reduction than CBT. 41.7% had >=30% reduction vs 1 CBT patient.

key_trials.citation: Yarns BC, Jackson NJ, Alas A, Melrose RJ, Lumley MA, Sultzer DL. JAMA Netw Open 2024. PMID 38869899 (not Schubiner-authored)
key_trials.design: RCT. EAET vs CBT. Older veterans with chronic musculoskeletal pain.
key_trials.finding: EAET superior on pain severity at post-treatment and 6 months. >=30% pain reduction in 63% vs 17%. Also better on anxiety, depression and PTSD symptoms.

key_trials.citation: Maroti D, Lumley MA, Schubiner H, et al. J Psychosom Res 2022;163:111068. PMID 36327532
key_trials.design: RCT. 10-week self-guided internet EAET vs waitlist. Somatic symptom disorder.
key_trials.finding: Reduced somatic symptoms at post-treatment and 4 months. Effects on pain, depression and anxiety were not retained. About 20% substantially improved.

key_trials.citation: Ashar YK, Gordon A, Schubiner H, ..., Wager TD. JAMA Psychiatry 2022;79:13-23. PMID 34586357 (5-yr follow-up JAMA Psychiatry 2025;82:1049-51, PMID 40736996)
key_trials.design: RCT. Pain Reprocessing Therapy (developed by Alan Gordon) vs open-label placebo vs usual care. Chronic back pain.
key_trials.finding: 66% pain-free or nearly so vs 20%/10%. g=-1.14 vs placebo. Maintained at 1 year.

key_trials.citation: Krohner S, Town J, Cannoy CN, Schubiner H, Rapport LJ, Grekin E, Lumley MA. J Pain 2024;25:39-52. PMID 37479050
key_trials.design: RCT. Single remote EAET/ISTDP-based interview vs waitlist. Chronic musculoskeletal pain with childhood adversity.
key_trials.finding: No difference in pain severity (primary). Greater reduction in pain interference and some mediators.

key_trials.citation: Crouch TB, ..., Ashar Y, Schubiner H, ..., Chelimsky T. Res Sq preprint 2026. PMID 42856466
key_trials.design: Non-randomised open-label pilot. PORT (n=14) vs community care (n=15). POTS.
key_trials.finding: Feasible (83% retention). Greater symptom improvement than community care. Not peer-reviewed.

controversy: One brain-learning mechanism is extended to fatigue, POTS, bladder, skin, anxiety and depression, beyond the trial evidence (mostly musculoskeletal pain, fibromyalgia, IBS and SSD). No trials test the branded book or course. Nearly all trials are co-authored by Schubiner, who earns from books, the course company and consulting; the main exception is Yarns 2024 (Lumley group). The 2017 fibromyalgia EAET trial (N=230) had a null primary outcome vs education. Krohner 2024 was null on pain severity. Diagnosing primary pain from history features (88% of back pain called primary) risks missing disease. The Sarno repressed-emotion framing is contested and can feel blaming to patients, and ME/CFS and long-COVID communities object to brain-based framings.

indicators.value: Self-published editions from 2010 (first edition year not re-verified); two self-published workbooks; Penguin Random House / The Open Field hardcover 26 May 2026 (448 pp, 14 h 6 min audiobook)
This Might Hurt (dir. Kent Bassett & Marion Cunningham) follows three patients in Schubiner's program; community screenings and CME/CE credit; release c. 2022 (year not stated on site)
Freedom From Chronic Pain 30-module course with forum; ~2% refund rate claimed; company existed by 2021

popularity.reach_estimate: ~100k-500k cumulative (order 10^5). Likely tens of thousands to low hundreds of thousands of book and workbook readers across editions since 2010 (sales not public), ~10k Coursera learners, thousands of clinic and online-course patients, and a documentary audience.
popularity.method_notes: The trajectory is anchored on documented events: the clinic in the 2000s (estimated), the book and first RCT in 2010, EAET trials 2016-2024, the PRT JAMA Psychiatry trial (Sept 2021 online / 2022) and the documentary (c. 2022), the online course company (by 2021), the Coursera MOOC, and the PRH trade edition (May 2026). The web-search quota was exhausted during both research and fact-checking, so Google Trends, Reddit subscriber counts and book sales were not retrieved. Levels are judged relative to these milestones and the publication record. The reach estimate is order-of-magnitude only.
